checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are accurate and rigorous. The taxonomy explicitly defines a 'switch' as a device with a faceplate, toggle/rocker, and specific mounting features. The generated image depicts an internal mechanical assembly (contacts, springs, housing) lacking all external user-interface elements defined in the checkpoints. Therefore, marking 8 out of 9 checkpoints as 'false' is correct. The only passing checkpoint ('Surface is smooth matte plastic') is technically true for the black housing but insufficient to establish class alignment given the missing structural components.
artifact_review: The Router identified structural implausibility in the metal strips (Severity 2) and texture issues on the blue block (Severity 1). I agree with these findings but believe the severity of the structural issue is underestimated. The metal strips appear to float without clear rigid attachment to the main body, which is a significant physical inconsistency (structural collapse/fusion). The Topology Auditor's high mask confidence (0.98) indicates the model sees a coherent shape, but this does not validate the physical realism of the thin, floating connections. The Perceptual Quality Auditor found only slight compression, missing the structural nuance. The Fine-Grained Classifier's failure to rank 'switch' as #1 (ranking 'spatula' and 'combination lock' higher) strongly supports the conclusion that the image lacks defining switch features.
alignment_reasoning: Severe misalignment. The image fails to meet the core definition of the target class (consumer electrical switch) by omitting the faceplate, actuator, and standard form factor. It resembles a generic mechanical component or internal mechanism. The classifier's top prediction of 'spatula' confirms the visual ambiguity and lack of class-specific features.
artifact_reasoning: Moderate artifacts. The primary defect is the physically implausible geometry of the thin metal contact strips, which appear to float or merge ambiguously with the housing (structural collapse). The blue insulator block exhibits waxy textures and illegible markings (texture anomaly/text gibberish). While the overall image is sharp, these structural and textural inconsistencies indicate AI generation flaws.
